title: Greg Cosell's 2026 NFL Week 8 PREVIEW: Part 2 + Panthers - Packers REACTION
transcript_summary: Ross Tucker and Greg Cosell preview the upcoming NFL slate, analyzing offensive and defensive schemes including the Bears vs Seahawks, Chiefs vs Broncos, Eagles vs Commanders, and Rams vs Chargers. In Tuck's Takes, Ross and Producer Jack recap Green Bay's victory over Carolina and Jordan Love's standout performance.

analysis_notes.summary: Raiders offense relies heavily on 12 personnel with Bowers, but total inability to establish a run game puts excessive pressure on the passing game when forced into 11 personnel from behind.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: their total inability to run the ball is really hurting them.

analysis_notes.summary: Browns run the league's highest percentage of single-high safety and Cover-1 with a heavy stunt-front concept; Jim Schwartz compared Carson Schwesinger's rookie vision and game diagnostic ability to Ray Lewis.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: they play the highest percentage of single high safety in the league, they play the highest percentage of cover one in the league.

analysis_notes.summary: Buccaneers generated 250 rushing yards behind a dominant offensive line and three-headed backfield led by Bucky Irving, allowing Baker Mayfield to throw only 11 times.
analysis_notes.speaker: Ross Tucker
analysis_notes.quote: the Bucs just ran over the Carolina Panthers... Baker only had to throw it 11 times.

analysis_notes.topic: Rams Run Game Tandem vs Chargers Scheme Fit
analysis_notes.summary: Rams rely heavily on Kyren Williams for downhill interior duo schemes and Blake Corum for outside zone edges; questions linger over whether Mike McDaniel's offensive system aligns with Justin Herbert's skill set.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: Kyren Williams, he's a square your shoulders downhill guy... Corum you can run a little more outside zone with.

analysis_notes.topic: Broncos Empty Formations & Seahawks Blueprint Myth
analysis_notes.summary: Seattle stifled Kansas City out of a base 2-high shell without stacking the box; Sean Payton frequently utilized Bo Nix in empty sets to force defense declarations, leading to big chunk plays to Courtland Sutton.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: the Seahawks played almost the entire game out of their normal two-shell coverage... Sean Payton lines up in empty and has Nix throw.

analysis_notes.summary: Eagles defensive front produced a poor performance; Jalen Carter was pushed around by interior guards, Jordan Davis remains a non-factor on 3rd down pass-rush snaps, and Jihaad Campbell's misread fits hurt run defense.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: that was as bad a performance by their defensive front as I think we've seen.

analysis_notes.topic: Caleb Williams Arm Arrogance vs 2-High Zone
analysis_notes.summary: Caleb Williams displays exceptional 'arm arrogance' by ripping throws into tight zone windows against 2-high safety structures, highlighted by a precise back-shoulder throw to Rome Odunze against Marcus Jones.
analysis_notes.speaker: Greg Cosell
analysis_notes.quote: Williams has tremendous arm arrogance... he will turn it loose against zone, he will throw into tight windows.

analysis_notes.summary: Jordan Love played outstanding football despite minimal run support and kicking blunders in Green Bay's 27-19 win; Carolina's offensive line surrendered constant pressure on Bryce Young.
analysis_notes.speaker: Ross Tucker
analysis_notes.quote: Jordan Love was outstanding again last night... Bryce Young was under siege again.
